record.summary: Creates the Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act. Using generative AI is no defense to a consumer-protection violation; under the 2025 revisions in S.B. 226, a supplier must disclose that a consumer is dealing with AI when asked clearly, and providers in regulated occupations must disclose high-risk AI interactions. The Act sets up an Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and an AI Learning Laboratory Program in which regulatory mitigation agreements can be granted for AI pilot testing. It is scheduled to be repealed on 1 July 2027.
record.notes: Signed 13 Mar 2024; takes effect 1 May 2024 (Section 13 of the enrolled bill). S.B. 149 first enacted the Act as Title 13, Chapter 70, with its liability rule in section 13-2-12; the Act now sits in Title 13, Chapter 72. S.B. 226 (2025) repealed section 13-2-12 and enacted Chapter 75, which keeps the liability rule and limits proactive disclosure to high-risk AI interactions in regulated occupations, with disclosure to consumers on a clear request; effective 7 May 2025. S.B. 332 (2025) extended the repeal date of the Act from 1 May 2025 to 1 Jul 2027. H.B. 452 (2025) added Chapter 72a on mental-health chatbots. H.B. 320 (2026) amended the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and the AI Learning Laboratory Program provisions; effective 6 May 2026.

judgment.status_reasoning: The Act took effect 1 May 2024. Enrolled S.B. 332 moves its repeal from 1 May 2025 to 1 July 2027 and S.B. 226 carries the same change; 18 Oct 2026 is before 1 Jul 2027, so the Act is still in force.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific state law; clearly in scope.

open_questions: The stored texts of S.B. 226, S.B. 332, H.B. 452 and H.B. 320 are enrolled copies; no stored page shows the governor's signature or the legislature's final vote on them, so their enactment rests on the enrolled copies with stated effective dates.

The earlier note that a further Utah AI transparency bill stalled after White House pressure linked to EO 14365 (Axios, Feb 2026) is not supported by any stored source and was left out of the notes; it concerns a different bill.
